description: Unified monotax regime combining tax and social security into a single flat payment with a progressive, stepped contribution scale (25% in Year 1 to 100% in Year 4).
impact: Contributed to halving national informality over two decades; covers ~23% of target population.

description: Monotax mechanism consolidating taxes into one flat monthly payment for micro-entrepreneurs (MEI pays 5% min wage). Rural subsistence farmers contribute 2.1% of gross sales value.
impact: MEI registrations rose from 33% to 41.7%; 10.6M workers covered under MEI; 1 in 4 own-account workers protected under rural pensions.

scheme: Mandatory Insurance for Self-Employed (Inversely Proportional Subsidies)
description: Categorized contribution scale based on reference income brackets, where state matching subsidies are inversely proportional to worker income.
impact: Self-employed pension coverage rose from 15.9% to 44.8%; health coverage rose from 30.5% to 59.0%.

description: Low flat-rate monthly contribution tiers (70, 100, or 300 THB/month) accompanied by matching state co-contributions for informal and gig workers.
impact: Enrolled millions of informal workers across agriculture, trade, and transport.

scheme: Mandatory Social Security Fund for Non-Wage Earners
description: Unified mandatory social insurance scheme for non-salaried workers allowing a gradual 3-year scale-up of contribution bases for new entrants.
impact: Reached 1.7 million affiliated self-employed members by 2017 (up from 1.28M in 2013).

description: Voluntary pension savings mechanism supported by an annual state matching incentive (up to RM 250) for self-employed and gig workers.
impact: Significantly increases savings returns and financial value proposition for low-income gig workers.

scheme: Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) & CPF Transition Support
description: Provides quarterly cash payouts and CPF top-ups for low-income self-employed citizens, paired with temporary state transition subsidies.
impact: Buffers lower-income self-employed workers against contribution shocks while building long-term balances.

description: Unified special tax regime for micro and small enterprises providing temporary tax reductions (30% in Year 1, 20% in Year 2) to incentivize formal social insurance registration.
impact: Contributed to a 4.3% annual reduction in informal employment.

description: Unified simplified tax and contribution regime for small independent workers, combining income tax, VAT, and social security into one flat monthly fee.
impact: Tripled registered micro-entrepreneurs and improved social insurance access for vulnerable workers.

scheme: NHIS Earmarked VAT Levy & Informal Flat-Rate
description: Tax-financed health insurance system funded through an earmarked 2.5% VAT levy (NHIL) and flat-rate informal worker contributions with indigent exemptions.
impact: Covered over 40% of the national population, dramatically reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure.

description: Simplified turnover tax/contribution regime with reduced rates (1% for commercial, 2% for services) paired with state-backed micro-credit guarantees.
impact: Registered over 200,000 auto-entrepreneurs within three years of rollout.

scheme: Voluntary Social Security Scheme for Self-Employed
description: Flexible contribution calculation options based on declared reference wage brackets for self-employed and informal workers.
impact: Gradually expanding social security coverage outside formal wage employment.

description: Flexible income assessment policies permitting temporary opt-outs or scaled contribution rates for seasonal agricultural laborers during low-harvest periods.
impact: Protects seasonal workers from drop-outs due to severe agricultural income volatility.

agency: General Authority for Social Insurance & MLSP
description: Single-window delivery hubs delivering 21 services, mobile units for remote nomadic herders, and non-cash contribution payments (livestock/raw materials) via herder cooperatives.
impact: OSS regularly used by 60% of population (1.8M people); herder coverage boosted by 5–10%.

description: Mobile registration platform for rural agricultural women utilizing voice activation technology to overcome illiteracy and enabling airtime/mobile money contributions.
impact: Enrolled thousands of previously unreached agricultural women before transitioning them to state schemes.

description: Streamlined business and social security registration hubs located in high-density areas (e.g., municipal markets) equipped with integrated IT.
impact: Social security coverage increased from 39.8% to 55.3% between 2016 and 2020.

description: Physical micro-contribution saving boxes installed at transport terminals allowing informal workers to save small daily cash deposits, supported by UMID smart cards.
impact: Registered and collected contributions from over 107,000 informal transport workers.

scheme: e-Shram Portal (National Database of Unorganised Workers)
description: Centralized digital single-window portal that simplified registration for informal, gig, platform, and street workers using Aadhaar-linked verification.
impact: Registered over 280 million informal workers, providing portable social security identity.

description: Comprehensive mobile app enabling self-employed workers to register, change clinics, pay contributions via e-wallets, and access digital health cards.
impact: Dramatically reduced physical branch visits and improved voluntary contribution compliance.

description: Mobile outreach units equipped with satellite technology deployed to remote rural communities to register informal and agricultural workers for social protection.
impact: Extended social protection access to millions of marginalized rural inhabitants.

description: Integrated multi-channel service delivery network combining physical offices, mobile units, call centers, and web portals for one-stop social protection access.
impact: Significantly reduced administrative overhead and travel time for informal and rural workers.

description: Non-governmental association acting as a 'virtual employer' to collect, consolidate, and transfer social security contributions for informal worker associations.
impact: Enabled thousands of informal street vendors and transport workers to access formal health and pension systems.

scheme: Evening Clinic Operating Hours for Domestic Workers
description: Extended public healthcare clinic operating hours to evening shifts (5:00 PM – 9:00 PM) specifically tailored to domestic workers' working hours.
impact: Removed major time-conflict barriers preventing domestic workers from seeking medical care.

description: Dedicated online portal allowing employers of domestic workers to register employees and calculate proportional monthly contributions in under 5 minutes.
impact: Expanded formal social security registration to over 50,000 domestic workers during initial rollout.

scheme: Firm Threshold Reduction & IDEA Union Partnership
description: Reduced mandatory NSSF firm registration threshold from 8 workers down to 1 worker, partnering with the IDEA union (tuk-tuk drivers and street vendors) for enrollment.
impact: Extended employment injury and health protection to micro-enterprises and informal transport workers.

description: Lowered mandatory social insurance contract duration threshold from 3 months to 1 month and established digital voluntary pension contribution channels.
impact: Broadened mandatory baseline coverage to short-term, casual, and seasonal laborers.

description: Recruited local community assistants equipped with mobile smartphone applications to register informal and migrant worker families directly at their homes.
impact: Overcame digital literacy and geographic distance barriers in hill and mountain districts.

description: Simplified registration framework offering a hybrid contributory and non-contributory registration track open to self-employed and domestic workers.
impact: Established initial formal social security coverage baseline in a young nation.

description: Accredited local informal worker associations and trade secretariats to act as authorized registration and collection intermediaries for self-employed workers.
impact: Decentralized enrollment away from formal state offices, increasing local trust.

description: Deployed mobile regional teams equipped with laptops and power generators to conduct temporary registration clinics in rural agricultural markets.
impact: Brought social security registration directly to remote vanilla and coffee farmers.

scheme: Auto-Entrepreneur Portal & Chèque Emploi Service Universel (CESU)
description: Ultra-simplified online declaration portal and standardized voucher system (CESU) for households employing domestic/personal care workers.
impact: Tripled registered domestic service relationships and virtually eliminated paper filing.

description: Mandatory expansion of social security to micro-enterprises (<5 workers) enforced through mobile inspection and registration teams.
impact: Registered tens of thousands of micro-firms and informal retail workers.

scheme: Operational Plan for Extending Social Security
description: Multi-channel communication campaign using TV, radio, newspapers, and workshops, paired with integrating social security education into primary school curricula.
impact: Created high public buy-in and foundational social security awareness among future workforce generations.

description: Recruits and trains peer-to-peer community agents (Kader JKN) who conduct door-to-door outreach, educate neighbors, register members, and collect contributions.
impact: Enhanced community trust, boosted voluntary compliance, and reduced branch visits.
sources: SPACE Summary; ASEAN Snapshot; ILO Guidebook

description: Deployed tailored awareness campaigns using simplified pamphlets, mobile roadshows, radio broadcasts, and seminars targeting construction MSEs and sawmillers.
impact: Reached 1,500+ construction workers; surveys showed 85–98% willingness to contribute once mechanisms were explained.

description: Attached colorful, easy-to-read informative brochures detailing domestic workers' legal social security rights directly to monthly household electricity bills.
impact: Achieved near-universal household reach across all socio-economic strata.

description: Integrated mandatory practical modules on social security rights, self-employed contributions, and labor health into technical/vocational secondary schools.
impact: Instilled early awareness of formal social insurance benefits among youth entering informal trades.

scheme: Mbao Pension & Free Health Screening Outreach Events
description: Organized community health fairs offering free ear, vision, and blood pressure check-ups for informal artisans (jua kali), combining health fairs with Mbao pension enrollment.
impact: Created immediate tangible value that attracted thousands of informal workers to pension briefings.

description: Legal regime requiring contracting companies that account for >50% or >80% of a self-employed worker's income to co-contribute 7%–10% toward social security.
impact: Rebalanced financial obligations fairly, granting workers access to unemployment, sickness, and occupational injury benefits.

agency: State Welfare Boards (e.g., Construction & Beedi Boards)
description: Sector-specific welfare boards funded by a statutory 1–2% levy/cess on commercial construction projects or production value ($1/1,000 beedis). Provides health, accident, maternity, and funeral benefits.
impact: Decoupled benefit financing from direct worker wages, securing social protection for millions of casual workers.

description: Mandatory scheme for self-employed artists/writers where worker pays 50%, commercial users pay a 30% user fee, and federal government subsidizes 20%.
impact: Achieved comprehensive pension, health, and long-term care coverage across self-employed creative professionals.

description: Landmark legislation creating a legal framework that mandates digital platform companies to co-contribute toward platform drivers' retirement (CPF) and injury insurance (WICA).
impact: Decouples gig work protection from standard employment contracts, establishing risk-sharing between platforms and workers.

description: Combines mandatory/voluntary occupational injury insurance with voluntary retirement savings, backed by government matching grants and bundled micro-insurance.
impact: Extends comprehensive injury and disability coverage to high-risk informal sectors like transport, delivery, and hawking.

description: Tailored benefit packages for informal economy workers combining long-term pension savings with short-term protections like weather index insurance against drought.
impact: High worker enthusiasm due to the immediate relevance of climate/seasonal risk protection alongside pension savings.

description: Specialized social insurance branch tailored for smallholder farmers and artisanal fishermen, providing primary healthcare, maternity benefits, and invalidity/old-age pensions.
impact: Protects rural agricultural families through community-based dispensaries and solidarity contributions.

scheme: Ejo Heza Long-Term Savings & CBHI Health Motivators
description: Combined long-term micro-pension savings scheme with short-term credit collateral features, supported by 45,000 community health workers driving health insurance (CBHI).
impact: Achieved over 80% national health insurance coverage and enrolled millions in Ejo Heza savings.

scheme: Convenios Colectivos de Seguro (Collective Insurance Agreements)
description: Legal mechanism allowing rural cooperatives, unions, and producer associations (min. 50 members) to collectively negotiate contribution rates, collect fees, and act as administrative intermediaries.
impact: Empowered rural workers through collective bargaining, serving as a vital bridge between state and rural populations.

scheme: Legislative Mandate for Informal Sector Seat (RA 11199)
description: Statutory requirement mandating that at least one member of the tripartite Social Security Commission explicitly represent informal sector workers.
impact: Institutionalized informal workers' voice in national social security governance.

description: Worker-driven collective scheme organized by FIWON chapters that pools informal worker contributions, self-organizes social insurance, and advocates with public authorities.
impact: Created a trusted, grassroots alternative for informal workers in low-trust/low-public-investment settings.

scheme: Municipal Waste Picker Group Insurance Partnerships
description: Grassroots waste pickers' trade union (KKPKP) advocated for municipal recognition, securing municipal budget subsidies for collective group health insurance.
impact: Demonstrated how collective worker organization and local government partnerships can bridge urban protection gaps.
